A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AssistMimic and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original physics-simulation experiments on Inter-X and HHI-Assist, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation experiments and reports revised generalist results alongside the specialist comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The policy architecture, initialization, retargeting, contact rewards, and distillation procedure remain the same. The head-height formula correction does not establish a changed method: v1 already describes upper clipping and gives a capped reward in Table 6.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Inter-X help-up motions, HHI-Assist caregiving settings, altered recipient dynamics, generated trajectories, and unseen supportive actions. V1's '60 motions (30 paired motions)' becomes '30 paired' motions without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Both retain the unsuccessful Phys-Reaction rollout attempt, Kinematic-Recipient comparison, Frozen-Recipient/Sequential Training baseline, and identical ablated variants. Generalist comparisons still evaluate AssistMimic with and without DAgger.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix C specifies 2k PPO iterations per specialist and 1k distillation epochs. V2 Appendix D retains 2k for specialist comparisons but specifies 9k for specialist teachers and 4k for DAgger, substantially revising reported training budgets. However, its Generalist training paragraph still says 1k epochs, leaving the intended distillation budget inconsistent.

E4.justification: The component ablations, recipient-dynamics robustness tests, COM stability analysis, and qualitative failure analyses are retained. Appendix C expands the explanation of the existing COM analysis without adding a test; consolidating failure illustrations preserves the examined failure mode.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. COM standard deviation measures temporal movement within an episode, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Generalist results change substantially between v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 4: without DAgger, SR/MPJPE changes from 39.8%/103 mm to 77.3%/132 mm; with DAgger, from 64.7%/106 mm to 94.7%/168 mm. These are replacement results under revised reported training budgets, not verified same-setting gains. Specialist Tables 2–3 and the relocated COM values are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix D.2 defines the head-height reward using max(h, h_max); v2 Appendix E.2 changes this to min(h, h_max), correcting the expression to impose an upper cap. V2's COM equation explains the existing standard-deviation metric; it introduces no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The introduction revises its headline HHI-Assist success claim from 66% to 73%. The central novelty claim, multi-agent formulation, three methodological contributions, and claimed application scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 Appendix C explicitly explains that excluding failed or early-terminated episodes avoids artificially low COM variance. Section 4.6 also links visual observations to robustness against changing partner states. Existing explanations involving hand dexterity, recipient weight, retargeting limitations, and simulation-to-real transfer remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses a 9k-iteration budget for direct generalist training, distinguishes comparison specialists from distillation teachers, and specifies mass-weighted COM computation. These are localized documentation changes; the conflicting 4k and 1k distillation instructions reduce reproducibility. Table 6 hyperparameters and diffusion-planner implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 36 works and retain the same positioning relative to single-person control, kinematic interaction synthesis, and multi-agent reinforcement learning. Citation relocation and reference-page updates do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 condenses experimental descriptions and the conclusion, combines failure cases and limitations, corrects wording and cross-references, and introduces a dedicated COM appendix section. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The COM table moves from main-text Table 4 to appendix Table 5. V1 Figures 7–8 are consolidated into v2 Figure 7, with two of the four failure snapshots omitted. Captions and surrounding layout are compressed; the principal diagrams and remaining qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: The COM explanation and head-height formula correction improve clarity, but v2 introduces contradictory DAgger budgets of 4k and 1k epochs in Appendix D. Its higher generalist success rates accompany revised training budgets and larger position errors, so they do not establish a controlled performance improvement. The documentation benefits and new reproducibility inconsistency prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
